Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, if that's okay. You have my claim number.
Q: That works. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in a parking lot in League City, Texas, near the grocery store entrance. I was pulling into an open space.
Q: What time of day was it, and what were the weather and lighting like?
A: It was late afternoon. It was clear and dry, and the sun was low, so there was some glare on the windshield.
Q: Describe how the other vehicle came into contact with yours.
A: I had nearly stopped in my space when a white SUV backed out from the space across the aisle. It didn't look like
the driver saw me. Their rear bumper hit my front driver's side fender.
Q: Did you have any warning before the impact?
A: Just a horn tap from me, and then the impact. I braked as hard as I could but there wasn't time.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt, and did your airbags deploy?
A: Yes, I had my seatbelt on. The airbags did not deploy.
Q: Have you sought medical attention since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care the same evening. They diagnosed a neck and back strain and told me to rest and take
anti-inflammatories.
Q: How are you feeling now?
A: The neck stiffness is still there, especially when I turn my head to check traffic. My lower back aches after sitting for
long periods. I've been doing the exercises the clinic gave me.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm cooperating fully and I'll send any treatment records you request.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
